note: WHAT THE DAILY ATTENDANCE REPORT SHOWS, column by column. These are the columns SmartPRS 2's attendance report prints; a tenant chooses which of them appear on the daily view and in the export from Organization Setup / Configuration → Attendance report, and the choice is versioned in module_customisations under the key below. Every column's VALUE comes from the same settlement the muster and payroll use — this file only decides which of them are printed, never how one is computed.
max_range_note: Widest span the muster will settle in one screen or export — every employee's punches for the whole range are read fresh (see the ponytail note on AttendanceReport's class docblock). 366 covers a full year, so a tenant can pick any period up to 12 months rather than being held to single calendar months. Raise it here if this tenant's employee count still renders comfortably at a wider span; there is no cap on the underlying settlement itself, only on how much this one screen tries to draw at once.

team_leader.label: Reporting Manager
team_leader.note: Owner, 23 Sep: 'the Team Lead should read as Reporting Manager for more clarity for entire employee list'. The hierarchy is Employee -> Team Lead -> Manager -> Director and every step of it is reporting_manager_id, so one heading that is true for an agent, a team lead AND a manager beats one that is right only for the bottom row. Resolves reporting manager first, then a leader named on the team, then the legacy text column (AttendanceReport::reportingManagerOf).

reporting_manager.label: Reporting Manager
reporting_manager.note: The STRICT reporting_manager_id only, with no fallback. On an install whose hierarchy is the reporting line this shows the same value as 'team_leader' above, so ticking both prints the same name twice — pick one. Kept because a tenant who uses the teams register wants the two to differ.

shift.label: Shift
shift.note: ALWAYS ON. Late By, Early Exit and Overtime on the same row are all measured against the shift, so a row that omits it says 'late by 42' without saying late for what. Not the tenant's to untick — see the `always` handling in AttendanceReport::columns(). It sits immediately after `date` because that is where the reader is looking when they ask 'against what?'.

status_labels_note: How a status prints on the daily view. ON_LEAVE prints as Leave, as asked: an approved leave request marks the day automatically, nobody types it.
columns_order_note: The order columns print in is the order they are declared here. AttendanceReport::columns() walks this map in order and a tenant's saved choice is a SET of codes, never an order — so moving an entry in this file moves the column for every tenant, including ones who have already chosen their columns. `logs` is deliberately LAST: it carries the row's actions (Log, and Edit for a deciding role) and actions belong at the end of a row.
columns_always_note: A column marked "always": true is printed for every tenant regardless of the column choice they have saved. It exists because a saved list is a snapshot of the columns that existed when Save was pressed and nothing reconciles it afterwards — without this, a column added or promoted later can never reach a tenant who has already configured the screen. Use it only for a column the report cannot honestly be read without.
